provenance: co-authored (Kavik + Claude), 2026-11-03. Design: communities act locally; AI nodes match and propose; humans in each community decide. Government action is an optional parallel input, never a prerequisite. Asterisks = thin volume. Every row PROPOSED unless stated.

node_concentration(): flags any AI node brokering > 50% of accepted exchanges*
corroborate()/single_node(): marks proposals no second node reproduced
risks.status: PARTIAL: detector + consent gate; no structural guard against capture of the human gate itself

in_code: to_paper(): one-line paper/voice form of every proposal
risks.status: PARTIAL: degraded format exists; no channel tested

holdings only enter through a community's own file; propose() cannot change holdings
consent() returns a new record; old record unchanged
risks.status: PARTIAL: tamper-evident, not tamper-proof; a node can still append FALSE records. No experiment listed (gap); D3 corroboration + B6 quarantine added

in_code: schema_version on every profile and proposal; propose() refuses mismatched profiles
plain_ok(): every record and log line must carry a plain-language line
risks.status: PARTIAL: version mismatch caught; same version read differently is not

risks.status: OPEN: nothing in code; needs drills

risks.text: Compounding error across communities: one bad junction propagates network-wide
risks.status: OPEN here. Link: thermodynamic-accountability-framework assembly_instrument status.py CAUTION + checkout.py print field warnings before any method is handed on

risks.text: Outside actors: any devastation draws outside agendas (states, groups, profiteers) exploiting desperation -- funding/arming factions, disinformation, poisoned field reports, buying influence via aid. Standing variable, not edge case.
in_code: defenses.aid_status(): flags control terms attached to outside aid (D4)*
defenses.claim_status(): >= 2 independent sources to act (D3); claims about another community need direct contact with it (D5)

backups.text: AI link down: same records on paper, carried by runners or read over voice radio
Node compromised: append-only hash chain; other nodes reject unchained edits
Schema mismatch: plain-language fallback line on every record
No network at all: each community runs standalone on its own L0/L1 holdings
backups.in_code: cli.py gaps / order run on one community file with no network

backups.text: Human override always: any community can refuse an AI-proposed exchange
backups.in_code: consent(), state(): one refusal is final

experiments.question: What structural guard stops R1: rotation, multiple independent AI nodes, consent gates?**
experiments.cleanest_test: Tabletop over N rounds with 2+ independent AI nodes and rotating human sign-off; record node_concentration() and how often humans refuse or override.
experiments.null: Concentration and refusal rate are the same with one node as with several: multiplicity is not a guard.

experiments.question: Which low-power comms hold for months: mesh, packet radio, satellite (winter)?
experiments.cleanest_test: Run each channel unattended through a northern winter on its own power; log daily delivery of a fixed test message.
experiments.null: Delivery collapses within weeks on every channel: plan around runners and B1.

experiments.question: Will people under stress send the one line?**
experiments.cleanest_test: During a scheduled outage drill, count FR1/exchange lines sent per task handed out.
experiments.null: Return rate near zero: the loop is open in practice; status must stay UNCONFIRMED-heavy.

experiments.question: How much holdings detail to share vs keep local (R6)?**
experiments.cleanest_test: Same tabletop run at three detail levels (yes/no; coarse bands; quantities); compare match quality against the exposure each level creates.
experiments.null: Yes/no matches as well as quantities: never share quantities.

experiments.question: Which pre-event trust agreements between communities actually hold?
experiments.cleanest_test: Compare drilled vs signed-only vs no agreements in a multi-community exercise; record exchanges completed and refused.
experiments.null: No difference: agreements are paper; build trust some other way.

experiments.question: Matching performance: AI vs human coordinators on the same scenario
experiments.cleanest_test: Identical scenario; arm A uses coordination.py propose, arm B human coordinators only; score gaps closed, time, refusals.
experiments.null: Humans match as well or better: AI layer adds risk (R1-R7) without benefit.

experiments.question: Historical cases of outside exploitation in disasters/collapse (Bosnia, Somalia, others) -> pattern library of entry methods**
experiments.cleanest_test: Code each documented case with one fixed form (entry channel, what desperation it used, how long before visible, what stopped it); kept at the level of entry channels for defenders, not operational detail.
experiments.null: No entry channel recurs across cases: a pattern library adds nothing beyond case-by-case vetting (D2).

experiments.question: Detection signals: what early infiltration looks like in a small community**
experiments.cleanest_test: Tabletop with a hidden red-team actor among ordinary newcomers; vetters (D2) record signals blind; score signals against who was actually red-team.
experiments.null: Recorded signals do not separate red-team actors from ordinary newcomers: no reliable early signal; rely on D3/D4/D5 gates instead of detection.

experiments.question: Does manual capability survive with an AI layer present? (added for R5; first numbered E7, renamed E9 when the operator assigned E7)*
experiments.cleanest_test: Cut the AI layer mid-exercise without warning; time to resume on paper (B1) vs a team that never had it.
experiments.null: Resume time equal: no over-reliance detected.

experiments.question: Sybil gap in D3: does counting independence by distinct contact paths (not distinct ids) stop one actor running two ids, without blocking honest reports?**
experiments.cleanest_test: Tabletop: a red-team actor sends the same false claim under two ids; honest reporters send true claims, some through a shared radio relay. Score each claim under independence_mode='ids' and 'contact_paths'; count false claims reaching ACTIONABLE and true claims held at CAUTION_ONLY.
experiments.null: False-ACTIONABLE rate is the same in both modes (the actor just uses two paths), or contact_paths holds back as many true claims as it stops false ones: paths add cost without protection.

defenses.text: Activation: parallel community/state/federal activation lowers desperation and shrinks the recruitable surface
defenses.in_code: none (policy). gov_parallel_restoration stays a parallel input, never a prerequisite; D1 is why parallel activation still matters

defenses.text: Trust vetting: necessity-built trust-assessment skills (registry category) screen newcomers, aid offers, intermediaries
Ledger poisoning guard: single source can raise caution, never rewrite; corroboration from independent reporters required
defenses.in_code: defenses.claim_status() CAUTION_ONLY below ACT_MIN_SOURCES (2); independence_mode='contact_paths' is the default since decision T2 (E10 synthetic run); 'ids' still selectable; assembly_instrument/status.py (caution on one report, builds counted not reports). Threshold relation: decision T1

defenses.text: Aid provenance: tag every outside resource with source + conditions attached; flag aid that carries control terms
Info hygiene: claims about other communities need direct-contact confirmation before action (counters engineered inter-community distrust)

decisions.question: assembly_instrument TESTED needs 3 independent builds; D3 ACTIONABLE needs 2 independent sources. Drift or on purpose?
decisions.verdict: Different on purpose: acting vs certifying. Recorded here so a later change is a choice, not drift. PROPOSED (design choice, not measured).
ladder: 1 report/source: may WARN (D3 CAUTION_ONLY; assembly CAUTION on one field warning)
2 independent sources: may PROPOSE ACTION in this community; a person still consents (D3 ACTIONABLE)
3 independent builds: may CERTIFY a method TESTED for every community (assembly status.py DEFAULT_N)
why: Scope: an action is one community's, under its own consent gate (B5); a TESTED method travels to every community that checks it out (R7 compounding).
Duration: a claim about current state is perishable; waiting on a third source can cost the hours the claim is about. A method certification is durable and nothing is lost by waiting.
Reversal: a local action can be stopped by the same people who took it; a certified method has to be un-learned network-wide.
Independence keys differ too: builds are keyed by distinct (date, coarse region); claims by distinct source id (or contact path, E10).
decisions.open: Neither number is measured. E3 (return rate) and E10 bear on whether 2 and 3 are the right values.*

decisions.question: E10 synthetic run: should claim_status default switch from independence_mode='ids' to 'contact_paths'?

cases.a: red team: 1 false claim, 2 ids, 1 path. expect ids ACTIONABLE (wrong), paths CAUTION_ONLY (right)
cases.b: honest: 2 reporters, shared relay (1 path). expect ids ACTIONABLE (right), paths CAUTION_ONLY (delayed)
cases.c: honest: 2 reporters, 2 paths. expect both ACTIONABLE
cases.d: red team: 1 false claim, 2 ids, 2 real paths. expect both ACTIONABLE (known hole; E10 does not close it)

scores.false_act: a false claim that reaches ACTIONABLE
scores.delayed_true_act: a true claim that 'ids' makes ACTIONABLE and the other mode holds at CAUTION_ONLY (the warning still goes out; only acting waits)

weighting.meaning: one false ACT costs N delayed true ACTs
weighting.why: A false ACT moves people or stock on a fabricated claim; some of that cannot be undone (fuel burned, a road cut, trust between communities spent) and it is the exact effect R8 actors aim for. A delayed true ACT still had its warning out at CAUTION_ONLY, and the delay ends when a second contact path confirms. Delay can still cost hours on perishable claims, so N is kept low rather than large.
weighting.volume: thin***: N is a judgement, not measured; no outcome data on either cost

decisions.rule: loss(mode) = N * false_act + delayed_true_act, summed over cases a-d with one claim per case (equal weight). Switch the default to contact_paths if and only if N * (false_act[ids] - false_act[contact_paths]) > (delayed_true_act[contact_paths] - delayed_true_act[ids]). Otherwise the default stays ids.
stated_in_advance: With one claim per case and the expected outcomes above, the rule fires for any N > 1 (reduction 1 vs cost 1). So this run tests whether the CODE behaves as specified, not how often each case happens in the field. Real case frequencies are the tabletop E10, still NOT_RUN.

Unscored, recorded only: case e, honest reporters with NO contact paths written down. Under contact_paths such a claim can never reach ACTIONABLE until someone records the paths. This is a recording burden the scored cases do not price.
Case d stays an open gap whatever the rule says.

result.run: 2026-11-04, tests/test_e10.py (synthetic, code-level), after T2 was committed in 76cee5f
result.action: default independence_mode switched ids -> contact_paths in defenses.claim_status and the CLI. ids mode kept and selectable.
result.unscored_case_e: confirmed: honest claim with no recorded paths is ACTIONABLE under ids, CAUTION_ONLY under contact_paths
result.open: Case d (one actor, two real paths) passes in both modes. Real case frequencies untested: tabletop E10 still NOT_RUN.
